judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble parenthetically equates the terms "Fund" and "Plan" as a single label, and identifies five named individual Trustees; the equation of two words later given distinct technical meanings is a latent definitional slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 1.20 and 1.22 draw a sharp line between the "Plan" (rules) and the "Fund" (assets), which the preamble collapses, and Amendment No. 4 (c116) replaces the named Trustees entirely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short recital that defines "Collective Bargaining Agreements" loosely as agreements which "among other things, establish the Plan"; the wording is general but not genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the narrower operative definition in Section 1.8, which requires the agreement to be "acceptable to the Board," a limitation the recital does not mention.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely narrative recital; the only defect is the OCR misspelling "contenplate," which changes nothing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.1 and 3.3 on the Union and Association appointing Trustees; nothing to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Exclusive purpose of providing pension and retirement benefits to certain employees" uses the vague qualifier "certain," but the defined terms carry the work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital's "exclusive purpose" language must be read with Section 2.2 and Section 5.5(w) (collecting contributions for other plans) and Section 5.3 (paying administrative expenses), a mild recital-vs-operative tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple historical recital of amendment dates with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with Section 1.2's definition of the Agreement as amended and restated from time to time.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It cites "Paragraph 18 of the Trust Agreement" as the amendment power, but no Paragraph 18 exists in the restated instrument, a dangling cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The operative amendment power is Section 10.1, limited by Section 10.2, so the recital points to a source of authority the operative text has replaced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration clause; "promises" appears as "promises"/"promises" only through OCR, nothing substantive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No operative provision cuts against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The "unless the context otherwise requires" carve-out is boilerplate but by design lets defined terms be displaced, which is a soft edge rather than an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Section 12.7, which imports Plan definitions into this Agreement; together the two create a possible circularity about which definition governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining "Administrator" to mean the Board itself or any delegate makes the term shift referents depending on context.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.6 separately makes the Board the ERISA "administrator," and Section 7.1 assumes a distinct Administrator with its own functions, so the roles overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain self-referential definition of the instrument; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preamble and Section 12.17 on duration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition names the "Publishers' Association of New York," dropping "City" from the entity's actual name — a mechanical slip in an identifying term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble, Section 12.8(d) and the signature block all use "Publishers' Association of New York City," so the defined term does not match the party actually bound.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Both the Chairman and Secretary of the Board" is ambiguous as to whether the two must act jointly or each qualifies alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.15 authorises "the Chairman and Secretary" to execute documents while Section 12.6 makes an instrument executed by the Chairman alone conclusive, sharpening the same question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is partly circular — a Beneficiary is one "entitled under the terms of the Plan" — and "such other person or entity who, as a result of his relationship" is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers to the Plan, which is not before the reader, and Section 12.7 imports Plan definitions, so the boundary is set outside this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise definition tied to specific ERISA sections; no term is left at large.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes the Board both named fiduciary and ERISA administrator, which overlaps Section 1.1's separate "Administrator" and Section 7.1's allocation, but the allocation article resolves it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Internal Revenue Code of 1936" is a plain mechanical error: no such Code exists and the intended reference is 1986 (or 1954).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.3, 4.4, 10.1(b) and 5.7 all turn on "the Code" and its sections 401(a), 501(a) and 4975, none of which exist in a 1936 Code, so the error propagates through the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition sweeps in "participation agreement, or other written agreement," a catch-all after specifics, and adds the vague condition "acceptable to the Board."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.1 says contributions are governed solely by the Collective Bargaining Agreements, and Section 1.13 defines Employers by reference to such agreements, so "acceptable to the Board" can gate who is an Employer at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition that also carries operative substance (incorporation by reference, exculpation), but its terms are specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The incorporation is expressly subordinated to this Agreement where inconsistent, and Section 5.5(h) authorises the pooling, so the pieces fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite; "at least one Employer Trustee and one Union Trustee" is a clear floor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.6(b) requires each Committee to have "two or more Trustees" with equal numbers from each side, a stricter rule than the definition's one-and-one minimum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "An individual employed by an Employer who is covered under the terms of a Collective Bargaining Agreement" is definite in form, though "covered" does real work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It meshes with Sections 1.13 and 2.4(c) (employer designating categories of covered employment), with only ordinary interdependence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It cross-refers to "Corporate Trustee (as that term is defined in Section 3.12)," but Section 3.12 never defines the term, only uses it — a broken internal reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.12 treats the Corporate Trustee as a separate sole trustee, while this definition folds it into "Custodian," a role Sections 5.12 and 8.1(b) treat quite differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any employer required to contribute" is circular in a withdrawal-liability setting: the question is usually whether an entity is required to contribute at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.4 says any employer "acceptable to the Trustees" may participate and Section 1.8 conditions the CBA on Board acceptance, so several tests of Employer status coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer definition with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3(a) was replaced by Amendment No. 4, so the pointer now runs to amended text, but that is ordinary operation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard statutory definition; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the many ERISA references throughout, notably Sections 2.3 and 12.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is entirely by citation to ERISA 404(b) and 29 C.F.R. 2550.404b-1, which is precise even if the OCR mangles it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5(p) uses the term consistently with the same regulatory requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Written communications signed by an Authorized Person" is then said to include telex and "any other such system" where identity can be verified "with a reasonable degree of certainty" — the signature requirement and the electronic carve-out pull against each other and "reasonable degree" is vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.6 lets Investment Managers issue "Instructions" directly to broker-dealers and Section 8.2(a) requires specimen signatures, so the loosened form of Instruction matters elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but carefully structured definition tracking ERISA 3(38); the elements are enumerated and closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The final sentence letting the Board appoint the Custodian as Investment Manager sits oddly with Section 8.5's blanket disclaimer of liability for Investment Managers, but they can be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward segregation definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Sections 8.1(b) and 1.22, with no evident friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Plan" means detailed rules "from time to time adopted by the Board," a moving target but definitionally clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble uses "Fund" and "Plan" interchangeably, which this definition and Section 1.22 contradict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list introduced by "including, but not limited to" and closed by catch-all (k), with unmatched parentheses in the qualifying-employer-securities parentheticals — classic general-versus-specific scope risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5 grants powers over "Securities or other property," so the list's outer boundary rarely matters; the pieces cohere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The asset-based definition is clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with the preamble's use of "Fund" as a synonym for "Plan," and with Section 3.12(b) allowing a Corporate Trustee to hold "the Fund" as a trust "separate from the Fund created by this Trust Agreement."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "When acting as Trustees, their successors and assigns (if such Successor Trustees have been appointed)" is awkwardly conditional but yields a workable meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.9 and 3.10 supply the appointment mechanics referenced, so the definition is anchored.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "And any affiliates thereof" is an undefined extension of the party's identity, though brief.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble likewise binds the Union "and its affiliates," so the instrument is consistent on the point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pointer definition with nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3(b) is the referenced source and was replaced by Amendment No. 4; ordinary operation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A naming clause; nothing capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the preamble and Section 9.3's payee designation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Exclusive purpose of providing certain pension and related benefits" leaves "related benefits" undefined and the exclusivity qualified by the same sentence's financing purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1(a) lets the Board define "such other related benefits," and Section 5.5(w) allows collections for other plans, so the exclusivity language must be read down.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The self-executing "this Agreement shall be deemed amended in such fashion as will implement the purposes of this Trust" is vague about what the deemed amendment actually says.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with Section 10.1, which requires a unanimous Board vote to amend, and with Section 10.2's flat prohibition on certain amendments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any contributing Employer acceptable to the Trustees" makes participation turn on an unstated standard of acceptability.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.13 defines Employer without any acceptance requirement, and Section 1.8 puts acceptance at the CBA level, so three different gates on participation coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Shall be deemed to have ... agreed to be bound unconditionally" to all Trustee decisions is a sweeping deeming provision whose reach (past and future amendments) is contestable, and the lettered items are duplicative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Section 9.1's promise that nothing in the Trust Agreement changes the terms of any collective bargaining agreement, which is precisely what unconditional adoption would do.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The numbers are specific — two Employer and three Union Trustees — but that composition is inherently unbalanced in a jointly-administered fund.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.3's quorum of two of each and Section 6.2(b)'s "any four Trustees" fit awkwardly with a five-member board, and Amendment No. 4 replaced this section with a 2-2 composition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain acceptance-of-trusteeship clause with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the signature page and Sections 3.4 and 3.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare list of names; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Superseded by Amendment No. 4 (c118), which is the ordinary operation of the amendment power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "As soon as practicable" is a soft timing standard, but the obligation itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.9 and 3.10 require filing certificates with the Board, so the writing requirements dovetail.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: service until death, incapacity, resignation or removal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.8 as amended fixes Union Trustees as incumbent officers, which effectively adds loss of office as a terminating event not listed here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The last sentence deems a Trustee resigned when "the Contributing Employer which designated him" ceases to contribute, but no Trustee is designated by a Contributing Employer under this instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.1, 3.3 and 3.7 make the Association (not any individual Contributing Employer) the designating body for Employer Trustees, so the deemed-resignation trigger cannot operate as written.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "With or without cause" and immediate effectiveness on filing are unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligned with Section 3.9's successor mechanism; the asymmetry with Section 3.8 (Union Trustees not removable at will) is deliberate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading says "Removal" but the text mostly fixes who the Union Trustees are, and it provides for a successor to be "elected" only where an officer is "prevented ... by operation of applicable law" — a narrow, oddly drafted trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.10 says the Union's principal officer shall designate the successor while this section says one shall be elected from full-time officers, and Section 3.3(b)'s named trustees need not be the incumbent officers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear mechanism: certificate signed by an authorized Association officer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.1, 3.7 and 3.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section says the principal officer "shall designate" a successor and, in the same sentence, that "a Successor Union Trustee shall be elected from the full-time officers" — designation and election are inconsistent methods.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.8 makes the Union Trustees the incumbent officers automatically, which leaves no room for either designation or election in the ordinary case.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard vesting-of-powers clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Sections 3.4, 3.9 and 3.10 without friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence beginning "Notwithstanding such transfer, the Board ... functions under the Plan" is missing its verb, and "such other duties and powers as the Board may deem advisable" is an open catch-all after two specific delegations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Delegating power to hold the Fund "as sole trustee of a trust separate from the Fund created by this Trust Agreement" is hard to square with Section 1.22's definition of the Fund and with Section 5.1's vesting of all title in the Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Such other related benefits as the Board may from time to time determine" is an open catch-all against the specifics "pension, retirement," and "-Iay" for "may" is a typographical slip in the operative restriction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2 confines the Trust to "certain pension and related benefits" and Section 5.14 gives the Board sole discretion to construe, so the outer edge of permissible benefits is set by the Board itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short, definite sentences; the amendment and termination powers are stated without qualification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Terminate the Plan (at any time)" sits against Article 10's structured amendment and termination requirements (unanimous vote, Section 10.2's limits), which the unqualified grant here bypasses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single permissive sentence with a parenthetical clarifier; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.1(b), 5.3(b) and 5.4 on insurance contracts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lettered conditions are scrambled — clause (c) about deductibility appears after the closing sentence and clause (b) reads "the Plan status receives an adverse determination" — so the trigger conditions cannot be read in order as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.2 forbids any return or diversion of Fund assets to Contributing Employers except as provided in Section 10.3, yet this section authorises exactly such a return without cross-referencing 10.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is textually broken — the opening words are missing, sentences interleave, and the final clause lets the Board terminate payments "to the spouse, children and relatives" of a payee, which does not follow from what precedes it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its exceptions defer to "the Plan, ERISA or the Code," and Section 12.15 separately conditions any entitlement on a Board determination, so the anti-alienation rule interlocks with several other provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Vested with all right, title, and interest in and to such monies" is emphatic but plain; the receipt-and-hold obligation is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.12(b) allows the Fund to be held by a Corporate Trustee as sole trustee, which qualifies the vesting stated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two sentences directing payment per the written Plan; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers correctly to Section 4.2 and dovetails with Section 4.1(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All reasonable and necessary expenses ... including, but not limited to" seven enumerated categories is a general-plus-specific structure, and "reasonable and necessary" is a standard that must be applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (d) bars Trustee compensation while allowing reimbursement, which fits Section 7.2(8)'s expense-approval role; nothing genuinely conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but carefully drafted insurance authority with a clear non-party carve-out for carriers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with Sections 4.3, 5.3(b) and 10.3(c); insurers are consistently kept outside the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Twenty-five enumerated powers closed by (y), "perform all acts (whether or not expressly authorized herein) which the Trustees may deem necessary and prudent" — an unbounded catch-all against a long list of specifics, the paradigm ejusdem generis problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4(a) purports to give Investment Managers "the powers set forth in Section 5.5, except subsections (3) through (y)," a reference that does not match this section's lettering, and Section 5.13 limits delegation to "ministerial" powers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Including but not limited to responsibilities related to the acceptance and processing of benefit applications and delinquent employer contributions" is an open-ended delegation of fiduciary duties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.10 requires only one Trustee from each side while 5.6(b) requires two or more with equal numbers, and Section 5.13 confines delegation to ministerial powers — three overlapping delegation rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It tracks ERISA's prudent-man standard closely; the "clearly prudent not to do so" carve-out is statutory language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Section 5.9(b), which says Trustees are not personally liable for any error of judgment or any act or omission — an exculpation that would swallow this duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad protective language ("conclusive evidence of the truth and accuracy") but each element is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its no-duty-to-inquire rule cuts against Section 5.7's prudence obligation and Section 9.9's audit powers, though those can be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Except as may otherwise reimbursed by insurance" omits the verb "be," and subsection (b)'s blanket non-liability "for any loss arising out of any act or omission" contradicts subsection (d)'s fraud/gross-negligence carve-out within the same section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.7's prudence standard and Section 5.11's fiduciary-insurance requirement both assume liability that 5.9(b) purports to erase, and the opening ERISA saving clause leaves the residue uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific: bonding as ERISA Section 412 requires, with a discretionary power to require more.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.3's expense provisions and Section 5.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "To the extent not precluded by ERISA" is a clean qualifier and the coverage described is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with Section 5.9(d)'s indemnity "through the purchase of insurance or otherwise"; the two are complementary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deposit and signature-authority rules are stated concretely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.15's separate signature authority for the Chairman and Secretary and for designated employees overlaps but does not contradict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Ministerial powers or duties" is the operative limit and its boundary against discretionary or fiduciary functions is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.6(a) allows delegation of "fiduciary responsibilities" to Committees and Section 5.5(r) allows delegation of Plan administration duties, so this section's narrower limit does not fit the rest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Complete authority, in its sole and absolute discretion, to construe the terms of the Plan or this Agreement ... final and binding upon all parties affected thereby" — the reach of "all parties affected" (participants only, or contributing employers too) is the classic fight over such clauses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is hard to reconcile with Section 6.6 (deadlocked questions go to an arbitrator whose award binds as if unanimously adopted) and Section 9.10 (withdrawal-liability disputes determined only by arbitration), each of which removes construction from the Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Multiple alternative signing authorities are laid out, but each is specified; no term is left at large.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.6 makes an instrument executed by the Chairman alone conclusive in favour of third parties, whereas this section contemplates the Chairman and Secretary together (or an authorised pair).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The term ... shall commence on the date of their election and continues until their successors are elected" mixes tenses but conveys one meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fixes the Chairman as a Union Trustee, which matters for Section 6.6(a)'s duty to submit deadlocked questions to arbitration and for Section 12.6's conclusive-instrument rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any four Trustees" may call a special meeting — a number that, on a five-member board, is a near-unanimity requirement and, after Amendment No. 4, equals the entire board.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1 (as amended by Amendment No. 4 to two and two) leaves exactly four Trustees, so the special-meeting mechanism becomes unanimous consent, which subsection (d) already covers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, arithmetically definite quorum rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Under Section 3.1 there are only two Employer Trustees (and, after Amendment No. 4, only two of each), so quorum requires every Trustee, which strains Section 6.4(d)'s reference to failure of quorum at two consecutive meetings.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section says action must be "by unanimous vote of the Trustees" and then "by unanimous vote of the two units," which are different rules stated in consecutive sentences.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.1 requires amendment "pursuant to the unanimous vote of the Board," leaving open whether that means the unit rule here or literal unanimity of individuals.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Need not be verbatim" is a modest qualifier; the obligation is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 11.1(b)'s records obligations are separate and compatible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Chairman "shall submit" on any Trustee's request and any single Trustee may petition the district court; subsection (e) refers to "both parties" though the dispute is among Trustees of one board, and the court reference is truncated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mechanism Section 6.4(d) invokes, but its promise that an award binds "as though ... adopted by unanimous vote" sits against Section 5.14's grant of exclusive construction authority to the Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence — "Where the Administrator is a Trust Fund, subject to the terms of this Agreement..." — is grammatically incomplete and states no proposition; the section's governing rule is simply missing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.1 defines the Administrator as the Board or its delegate and Section 1.6 makes the Board the ERISA administrator, so the truncated allocation here leaves the split of responsibility with Section 7.2 unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Eighteen enumerated responsibilities closed by "Generally, exercise of those functions and responsibilities which the Board deems necessary and appropriate" — an open catch-all after specifics, with the list itself partly garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item (1) and (2) give the Board the right to "amend, modify or terminate this Agreement at any time," which contradicts Section 10.1's unanimous-vote requirement and Section 10.2's flat limits on amendment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three specific subsections on appointment, segregation and Board-directed investment; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (c) overlaps Section 8.4(b) almost word for word, which is redundancy rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concrete requirements: a Board certificate, identified authorised persons, a written agreement, agreed compensation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-references to Section 8.8 are accurate and consistent with Section 7.2(12)-(14).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The Board may require" an acknowledgment is permissive, whereas the definition it implements treats acknowledgment as a defining condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.18 defines an Investment Manager as one who "has acknowledged in writing to the Board" its fiduciary status, so making the acknowledgment optional here is in tension with the definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All of the powers set forth in Section 5.5, except subsections (3) through (y)" cites a subsection "(3)" that does not exist in Section 5.5's lettered list — a mechanical error that determines the scope of the exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5 is lettered (a) through (y), so the excepted range cannot be identified without construing this reference against that section; Section 8.1(c) restates the fallback rule in subsection (b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exculpation is broad but its terms and its carve-out for specifically assumed duties are stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its "notwithstanding anything to the contrary" override cuts against Section 5.7's diversification and prudence duty and Section 7.2(13)'s monitoring obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short subsections, both expressly subject to the investment management agreement; nothing open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.4(a) and 8.8's guideline mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence making the Board "solely responsible" for an Investment Manager's authority — brief but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reads awkwardly beside Section 8.5, which disclaims Board responsibility for an Investment Manager's acts, though the subjects differ (appointment terms versus performance).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "May (but need not) be delivered" and the anti-assumption proviso are clearly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2(10) makes promulgating investment directions a Board responsibility, which sits a little oddly with the disclaimer that issuing them assumes no management power, but they can coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Nothing in this Trust Agreement shall be deemed to change, alter or amend any of the terms or provisions of any such agreement" is a broad subordination clause whose scope (rates only, or all obligations?) is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 9.4(b), 9.5(b) and 9.7 impose interest, liquidated damages and fee liability that no collective bargaining agreement may contain, and Section 2.5 deems Employers unconditionally bound to the Trust's terms — a direct pull against this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short timing rule keyed to the collective bargaining agreement; nothing to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes the duration of the contribution duty entirely a matter of the CBA, which bears on Section 10.3(a)(3)'s automatic termination trigger but does not conflict with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Payee and "manner and form prescribed by the Board" are simple and administrable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 9.9's remittance-report requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Notwithstanding the preceding sentence" attaches to the sentence about collection costs being paid from the Fund, which the following text does not actually contradict, and (b)'s "greater of interest on, or twenty percent of" is elliptical about the interest period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sets interest "at a rate calculated in accordance with Section 9.5," and Section 9.5(b) as amended by Amendment No. 2 makes that rate discretionary, so the cross-reference no longer yields a fixed number; Section 9.7(c) restates the same liquidated-damages formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any expenses incurred in effectuating such payment (including, but not limited to ...)" is a general phrase followed by specifics, and "interest at a rate of 18 percent per annum" is stated without saying on what, from when, or whether it compounds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 2 replaces this text with a discretionary rate, Section 9.4(a) computes interest "in accordance with Section 9.5," and Section 9.7(b)-(c) build the court-award formula on the same method, so which rate governs which payment is a live cross-provision question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The defined term "unpaid contributions" is introduced by a parenthetical that follows a long compound antecedent, leaving it unclear whether it captures rules and guidelines as well as contributions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That defined term is then used in Section 9.7(a)-(c) to fix the amounts a court must award, so the imprecision here propagates into the remedy provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of five recoverable items is specific and tracks ERISA Section 502(g)(2); item (e) is the statutory equitable-relief catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It computes interest "in accordance with the method set forth in Section 9.5," which Amendment No. 2 converted into a rate the Trustees may set at their discretion, so the formula depends on an amended provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to "this Article IX" and then "this Article 9" in the same sentence, a numbering inconsistency, but the saving-of-rights meaning is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves court and other remedies generally, which is hard to square with Section 9.10's statement that withdrawal-liability claims "shall not become the subject of litigation in the courts."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All records deemed necessary by such persons" makes the scope of the audit obligation turn on the auditing party's own judgment, and "may charge an Employer for the cost" is unconditional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.3(a) says collection and administration expenses are paid from the Fund, while this section lets the Board shift audit costs to an Employer, a tension the instrument does not resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says such claims "shall not become the subject of litigation in the courts ... but shall be subject to determination only by arbitration," then closes by preserving the Fund's own right to sue in court — the exclusivity is one-sided and its scope ("any and all claims by third parties (including Employers)") is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.8 disclaims any waiver of the right to enforce in "any other type of proceeding" and Section 9.5(a) authorises court proceedings, so the arbitration exclusivity must be reconciled with those savings clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "At any time and in any manner" is then cut back by a proviso that the amendment be "not inconsistent with the purposes for which the Fund was established" — a standard whose boundary is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2(1)-(2) states the Board's right to amend or terminate "at any time" without the unanimity requirement or the three provisos imposed here, and Section 2.3 provides for deemed amendments with no vote at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition and its single carve-out are stated cleanly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.4 permits returning mistaken or non-deductible contributions to an Employer, which is a return of part of the Fund to a Contributing Employer not saved by the Section 10.3 exception named here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three alternative termination routes are enumerated, and (b)'s direction to distribute surplus "in a manner consistent, in their opinion, with this Agreement" leaves the residual disposition to the Board's opinion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Route (a)(2) lets the Union and Association terminate by joint resolution while (a)(1) requires a unanimous Board vote, and Section 7.2(1) says the Board may terminate at any time — three inconsistent routes to the same result.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three concrete recordkeeping duties, opened by a clear "unless otherwise delegated" qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.1(g) assigns record maintenance to the Administrator, which this section's delegation proviso accommodates rather than contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Such commercially acceptable valuation method or methods determined by the Board" leaves the valuation standard to the Board's choice, though "fair market value" anchors it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 11.1(c) requires the Board to maintain information enabling fair-market valuation, and Section 5.7 imposes prudence, so the discretion here is bounded elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The New York City metropolitan area" is a loose geographic boundary, but the operative effect (deemed location of the Board) is simple.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.8's addresses and Sections 6.6(e) and 9.10's New York City venue provisions all point the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional choice-of-law clause with an express ERISA-preemption carve-out; each element is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.10 likewise applies New York law "to the extent not superceded by ERISA," so the instrument is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.2 refers to signature on "any counterpart or copy hereof," consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Wherever required by context" and the gender/number rules are standard interpretive boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its instruction that headings not be used in construction sits beside Section 3.8, whose heading ("Removal of Union Trustees") does not match its content — a reason the rule matters but not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short designation sentence with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Section 12.1's deemed location and Section 12.8's addresses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Making every instrument "executed by the Chairman of the Trustees" conclusive as to authority is a strong, one-sided protection whose reach against a Fund challenging its own officer's act is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.15 vests execution authority in the Chairman and Secretary together (or an authorised balanced pair), so a Chairman-only instrument is conclusive under 12.6 yet unauthorised under 5.15.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It imports every Plan-defined word into this Agreement "except as otherwise expressly provided herein," which is broad but has an express priority rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 1 defines terms such as "Employer," "Covered Employee" and "Plan" itself, and Section 1.20 makes the Plan a document the Board may unilaterally amend, so Plan definitions could displace or circle back on Article 1's.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision breaks off mid-sentence ("as of the date on which it is"), so the deemed-receipt rule has no completion, and the Union's street number (41-18) differs from the Fund's (47-18) at the same building.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendments Nos. 1 and 3 replace subsections (a)-(d) and rename the addressee "Fund Director," a title used nowhere else in the instrument (compare Section 1.1's "Administrator").

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text begins mid-sentence with a fragment ("uhé Board) or any person claiming by or through them"), so the class of persons denied any interest cannot be identified from the provision itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.16 states a narrower version of the same rule "except as set forth in the Plan," while this provision conditions all entitlement on a Board determination, echoing Section 5.14's discretion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard no-employment-right and no-equity clause, qualified by "except as set forth in the Plan."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Section 12.15, which states the same denial in absolute terms without the Plan exception, a small inconsistency between adjacent provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Without limit as to time" subject to Article 10 is plain and internally qualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 10.3's automatic termination when no Employer is obliged to contribute is the express carve-out this section anticipates; they fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amendment recites that "the Plan is hereby amended" while in fact amending Section 12.8(b) of the Trust Agreement — a mismatch between the instrument named and the instrument changed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It substitutes "Fund Director" for "Fund Administrator," a title that has no definition anywhere, whereas Section 1.1 defines "Administrator" and Section 7.1 assigns that office duties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "18 percent per annum or such other interest rate that the Trustees deem appropriate given the circumstances" replaces a fixed rate with an open discretionary one, and the operative sentence is left visibly incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.4(a) and Section 9.7(b)-(c) both compute amounts "in accordance with Section 9.5," so after this amendment those cross-references point to a rate that has no fixed content.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward address substitution; the only oddity is the retained "Fund Director" label and the truncated Association address.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Together with Amendment No. 1 it supersedes Section 12.8(a)-(d), leaving the unamended deemed-receipt sentence of 12.8 still incomplete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The restated preamble carries a stray, orphaned "2. the following:" and again equates "Fund" and "Plan" as one label.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The equation of Fund and Plan contradicts Sections 1.20 and 1.22, and the four named individuals must be read with amended Sections 3.1 and 3.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The appointment of Trustees shall be selected by the provisions of Section 3.4" is a plain mechanical error — "selected" should read "governed" — in the sentence that fixes the appointment mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reducing the board to two and two leaves Section 6.3's quorum requiring every Trustee and Section 6.2(b)'s "any four Trustees" requiring the whole board to call a special meeting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare substitution of four names; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with amended Section 3.1's two-and-two composition and with Sections 1.14 and 1.25's pointer definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading still reads "Removal of Union Trustees" while the text fixes who the Union Trustees are, and "vice president/secretary treasurer" collapses two offices into one hybrid title.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.10 still says the Union's principal officer shall designate a successor, while this section says one shall be elected from the full-time officers, and Section 3.5's term-of-office rule does not list loss of union office.
